score_objections.objection: Sources support strong federal oversight of frontier models (Safety Review Office, CFIUS-style pre-deployment evaluations, data center reporting), but every King source frames it narrowly: safeguards 'would apply to only the very largest and most advanced models,' new laws should 'avoid discouraging innovation,' and the bill is titled to preserve American dominance. Combined with his heavy personal use of AI tools, this reads as targeted frontier-model guardrails rather than broad strict rules now. -2 is defensible but -1 fits the sourced language better.

The only china_chips evidence is one bullet in a cosponsored bill requiring know-your-customer standards for IaaS providers dealing with foreign persons. No source shows King taking a position on chip export controls, the Nvidia/China sales debate, or the diffusion rule. Directionally hawkish but too thin to place him; consider no position until a direct statement is found.
